examples.en: How do critics review that novel?

examples.ko: 선생님은 제 글을 솔직하게 평해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher gave me an honest review of my writing.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 노래를 어떻게 평했는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder how my friend judged my singing.

examples.ko: 사람들이 그 식당을 맛있다고 평하는 이유를 알겠어요.
examples.en: I understand why people say that restaurant is delicious.

examples.ko: 남의 외모를 함부로 평하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't carelessly comment on other people's looks.

examples.ko: 전문가들은 이번 경기를 아주 훌륭했다고 평했어요.
examples.en: Experts said this match was excellent.

explain: 그냥 '말하다'가 아니라 좋고 나쁨을 따져서 말할 때 써요. 보통 '~라고 평하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 말보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 많이 보여요. 대화에서는 '평가하다'나 '이야기하다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '말하다' (to say), it means giving a judgment about good or bad points. It usually appears as '~라고 평하다' and is seen more in writing and news than in speech. In conversation, people also use '평가하다' or '이야기하다'.

examples.ko: 요즘 돈에 궁해서 외식을 못 해요.
examples.en: I'm short of money these days, so I can't eat out.

examples.ko: 궁할 때 도와준 친구를 잊을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't forget the friend who helped me when I was in need.
He always smiles even when money is tight.
I helped a neighbor who was in a difficult situation.

examples.ko: 돈이 궁하다고 해서 아무한테나 빌리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even if you're short of money, you shouldn't borrow from just anyone.
I was asked suddenly, so I'm at a loss for an answer.

explain: '가난하다'와 달리 돈, 대답, 방법처럼 꼭 필요한 것이 모자라서 곤란한 상황에 초점이 있어요. '돈에 궁하다', '대답이 궁하다'처럼 '~에/이 궁하다' 꼴로 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '가난하다' (poor), it focuses on being in a tight spot because something you need, like money, an answer or a way out, is lacking. It is used in patterns like '돈에 궁하다' and '대답이 궁하다'.

examples.en: The apples are red and look delicious.
Plump grapes hang in bunches from the vine.
I bought some beautifully ripe peaches at the market.
The flowers were so lovely that I looked at them for a while.
Everyone envies her thick, beautiful hair.
The watermelons really look great this year.

explain: 갖고 싶거나 먹고 싶을 만큼 풍성하고 보기 좋은 모습에 써요. 과일, 꽃, 머리카락처럼 눈에 보이는 것에 잘 어울려요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '탐스러워요', '탐스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It describes things that look so full and lovely that you want to have or eat them, such as fruit, flowers or thick hair. It suits visible things. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: '탐스러워요', '탐스러운'.

examples.en: He doesn't covet other people's property.
He lost his friends by craving a high position.

examples.ko: 욕심을 부려 남의 것을 탐하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't be greedy and covet what belongs to others.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 돈만 탐해서 인기가 없어요.
examples.en: He only craves money, so he isn't popular.
He has never sought fame.
My little brother covets his older brother's toys.

explain: 갖고 싶어서 욕심을 낸다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 재물, 권력, 명예 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '욕심내다'가 더 편하게 들려요.
explain_en: It carries a negative feeling of greedily wanting something. It goes well with words like wealth, power and fame. In everyday talk, '욕심내다' sounds more casual.

examples.en: Business went well and the shop prospered greatly.
They say a family that prospers has a lot of laughter.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 신제품 덕분에 다시 흥하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to a new product, the company started to thrive again.
I hope my parents' shop prospers for a long time.
Rising and falling can happen in an instant.
The neighborhood that once flourished is quiet now.

explain: 반대말은 '망하다'이고, '흥하고 망하다'처럼 짝으로 자주 써요. 가게, 집안, 나라, 사업이 잘되어 번창할 때 쓰고 '번창하다'보다 입말에 가까워요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '망하다' (to fail), and the two often appear as a pair: '흥하고 망하다'. It is used for shops, families, countries and businesses that do well, and it sounds more spoken than '번창하다'.

en: to be disappointed; to feel hurt

examples.en: I'm really hurt that you forgot our promise.
If you say it like that, I feel hurt.
I felt hurt that my friend left without any word.

examples.ko: 생일을 모른 척하면 섭해서 말도 안 나와요.
examples.en: If you pretend not to know my birthday, I'm too hurt to speak.

examples.ko: 제대로 인사도 못 드려서 섭하실 거예요.
examples.en: You'll probably feel sad that I couldn't say a proper goodbye.
Please don't take it too hard.

explain: '섭섭하다'의 줄임말이라 대화에서 더 가볍게 들려요. 기대만큼 대해 주지 않아서 서운할 때 쓰고 '서운하다'와 비슷해요. '간섭하다'의 '섭'과는 상관없어요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '섭섭하다' and sounds lighter in conversation. You use it when someone doesn't treat you as well as you expected, similar to '서운하다'. It is unrelated to the '섭' in '간섭하다'.

examples.ko: 동생이 하루 종일 뚱해서 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: My younger brother has been sulky all day and isn't talking.

examples.ko: 왜 그렇게 뚱한 얼굴로 앉아 있어요?
examples.en: Why are you sitting there with such a sulky face?
He answered sullenly, as if he were upset.
The child who got scolded is sulking.

examples.ko: 표정이 뚱하고 말이 없어서 걱정이 됐어요.
examples.en: He looked sulky and silent, so I was worried.
My friend was late, so I was in a sulky mood.

explain: '뚱뚱하다'와는 전혀 다른 말이에요. 못마땅하거나 기분이 안 좋아서 말없이 퉁명스러운 표정이나 태도를 보일 때 써요. '뚱한 표정', '뚱하게 앉아 있다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is completely different from '뚱뚱하다' (fat). It describes a sulky, silent look or attitude when someone is displeased or in a bad mood. Common patterns are '뚱한 표정' and '뚱하게 앉아 있다'.

examples.ko: 잠을 못 자서 오늘 좀 맹해요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep, so I'm a bit spaced out today.
Don't sit there with a blank look on your face.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 가끔 맹해 보여도 똑똑해요.
examples.en: That friend sometimes looks dim but is actually smart.
I'm out of it in the morning, so I just sit there blankly.
I don't like it when people say I seem dim.

examples.ko: 너무 맹해서 길을 세 번이나 잘못 들었어요.
examples.en: I was so out of it that I took the wrong road three times.

explain: 정신이 없거나 멍하고 좀 어리숙해 보일 때 써요. 친한 사이에서 가볍게 놀리듯 말하기도 하지만, 남에게 하면 기분 나쁠 수 있어요. '멍하다'와 비슷한데 '맹하다'는 어리숙한 인상까지 줘요.
explain_en: It describes someone who looks spaced out and a little naive. Close friends may use it to tease lightly, but it can hurt if said to others. It is close to '멍하다', but '맹하다' also gives an impression of being a bit simple.

examples.en: An unrestrained lifestyle harms your health.
Because of a lack of restraint, my paycheck disappears quickly.
His lack of self-control shows in his credit card bill.
I ate with no restraint and gained weight.
My goal is to cut down on reckless spending.

examples.ko: 무절제한 게임 습관 때문에 늦게 자요.
examples.en: I go to bed late because of my unrestrained gaming habit.

explain: 반대는 '절제'예요. 먹기, 쓰기, 시간 쓰기처럼 조절해야 하는 일을 마음대로 할 때 써요. 주로 '무절제한 + 명사', '무절제하게' 꼴로 쓰고, 말보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '절제' (moderation). It is used when someone does things they should control, such as eating, spending or using time, however they like. It usually appears as '무절제한 + noun' or '무절제하게', and is more common in writing and news than in speech.

examples.en: My strength declined as I got older.
My grandfather's health has weakened, so he goes out less.

examples.ko: 한때 강했던 나라도 힘이 쇠하는 때가 와요.
examples.en: Even a once-strong country has a time when its power fades.
My eyesight is gradually getting worse, so I changed my glasses.

examples.ko: 병을 앓고 나서 체력이 많이 쇠했나 봐요.
examples.en: I guess my stamina dropped a lot after being ill.

examples.ko: 쇠해 가는 마을에 젊은 사람들이 돌아오고 있어요.
examples.en: Young people are coming back to the declining village.

explain: 기운, 힘, 세력이 약해질 때 써요. 반대말은 '흥하다'나 '성하다'예요. 보통 '기력이 쇠하다', '체력이 쇠하다'처럼 몸이나 힘 이야기에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when energy, strength or influence grows weaker. Its opposites are '흥하다' and '성하다'. It often appears in phrases about the body or strength, such as '기력이 쇠하다' and '체력이 쇠하다'.

examples.en: I prefer soft-boiled eggs to hard-boiled ones.
I made a sauce with fully ripe tomatoes.

examples.ko: 그 배우의 연기는 완숙의 경지에 올랐어요.
examples.en: That actor's acting has reached a level of full mastery.

examples.ko: 과일은 완숙이 되기 전에 따면 맛이 없어요.
examples.en: Fruit doesn't taste good if you pick it before it is fully ripe.
To hard-boil it, it takes about ten minutes.
It looks cool to watch him cook with such mature skill.

explain: 달걀은 '완숙'과 '반숙'을 짝으로 말해요. 과일이 푹 익은 것뿐 아니라 솜씨나 연기가 무르익은 것에도 써서 '완숙한 연기'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: For eggs, '완숙' (hard-boiled) and '반숙' (soft-boiled) are paired. Besides fully ripe fruit, it also describes skill or acting that has matured, as in '완숙한 연기'.

examples.en: I saw news that the stock price hit its lower limit.
This stock fell all the way to the lower limit yesterday.
If you sell at the lower limit, your loss is big.
The stock keeps hitting the lower limit, so I'm very worried.
Today it was the lower limit, not the upper limit.

examples.ko: 하한가로 떨어진 주식을 산 사람이 있대요.
examples.en: They say someone bought a stock that dropped to its lower limit.

explain: 주식에서 하루에 내려갈 수 있는 가장 낮은 가격을 말하고, 반대말은 '상한가'예요. 뉴스에서 '하한가를 기록하다'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In the stock market, it is the lowest price a stock can fall to in one day. Its opposite is '상한가'. In the news you often see '하한가를 기록하다'.

en: be charmed; be fascinated; be enchanted

examples.ko: 광고에 혹해서 필요 없는 걸 샀어요.
examples.en: I was lured by an ad and bought something I didn't need.

examples.ko: 그 말에 혹하지 마세요, 사기일 수 있어요.
examples.en: Don't fall for that, it could be a scam.
Many people were taken in by the sweet words.
I was tempted by the low price and regretted it.
Many people are charmed by his voice.
I'm easily swayed because I'm easily persuaded.

explain: 말이나 사람, 물건에 마음이 끌려 넘어갈 때 써요. 보통 '~에 혹하다' 꼴이고, 좋은 쪽보다 '조심해야 할 유혹'을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '솔깃하다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when your heart is drawn to something, such as words, a person or an item, and you give in. It usually appears as '~에 혹하다' and often describes a temptation to be careful about. A similar word is '솔깃하다'.

examples.ko: 동생은 스무 살인데 아직 앳돼 보여요.
examples.en: My brother is twenty but still looks youthful.
A young-faced new employee greeted me.
Her voice sounded so young that I thought she was a student.
My mother looks so young in the photo.
What's your secret to looking so youthful?

examples.ko: 얼굴이 앳되고 키도 작아서 어려 보여요.
examples.en: Her face looks youthful and she's short, so she looks young.

explain: 나이보다 어리고 풋풋해 보이는 얼굴이나 목소리에 써요. '앳돼 보이다', '앳된 얼굴'처럼 자주 말해요. '어려 보이다'와 비슷하지만 더 순하고 풋풋한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a face or voice that looks younger and fresher than the person's age. Common forms are '앳돼 보이다' and '앳된 얼굴'. It is similar to '어려 보이다', but it feels gentler and more innocent.

examples.ko: 선거 때가 되면 후보자들이 가가호호 찾아다녀요.
examples.en: At election time, candidates go around visiting every house.
Volunteers visited house after house and delivered lunch boxes.
I went door to door to greet my neighbors.

examples.ko: 직원이 가가호호 다니면서 설문 조사를 해요.
examples.en: A staff member goes door to door doing a survey.

examples.ko: 명절 저녁에는 가가호호 불이 환하게 켜져요.
examples.en: On holiday evenings, lights are on brightly in every house.

examples.ko: 신문 배달원이 가가호호 신문을 넣고 가요.
examples.en: The newspaper carrier drops a paper at each house.

explain: '집집마다'와 같은 뜻이지만 한자어라서 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 보여요. 보통 '방문하다', '찾아다니다', '돌다' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '집집마다'가 더 쉬워요.
explain_en: It means the same as '집집마다' (house by house), but as a Chinese-origin word it appears more in news and writing. It usually goes with verbs like '방문하다', '찾아다니다' and '돌다'. In everyday talk, '집집마다' is easier.

examples.en: I liked the house, so I made a provisional contract first.
I made a provisional contract and sent part of the deposit.

examples.ko: 가계약 후에 마음이 바뀌면 돈을 돌려받기 어려울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you change your mind after a provisional contract, it may be hard to get your money back.

examples.ko: 가계약이니까 본계약 전에 한 번 더 확인하세요.
examples.en: It's only provisional, so check once more before the final contract.

examples.ko: 다른 사람이 먼저 가계약을 해서 그 방을 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: Someone else made a provisional contract first, so I missed that room.
Be sure to keep a photo of the provisional contract.

explain: 집이나 방을 구할 때 본계약 전에 먼저 자리를 잡아 두려고 하는 계약이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '본계약'이에요. 가계약금을 보낼 때는 돌려받을 수 있는 조건을 문자나 문서로 남겨 두세요.
explain_en: This is a contract made before the main one to hold a house or room. Its counterpart is '본계약' (the main contract). When you send a provisional deposit, keep the refund conditions in writing or in a message.

examples.en: The supermarket is discounting processed meat products.
They're processed, so they last longer than fresh ones.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 수산물 가공품도 같이 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop also sells processed seafood products.

examples.ko: 아이에게는 가공품보다 신선한 과일을 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to give my child fresh fruit rather than processed food.
I check the ingredients of processed goods on the packaging.

examples.ko: 농산물 가공품 수출이 늘었다는 소식이 있어요.
examples.en: There is news that exports of processed farm products have grown.

explain: 원래 재료를 손질하거나 만들어 바꾼 물건이에요. 식품에서는 '가공식품'과 함께 많이 쓰고, 반대로 가공하지 않은 것은 '원재료'나 '생것'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to goods made by treating or transforming raw materials. For food it appears together with '가공식품', and unprocessed things are called '원재료' or '생것'.

examples.en: That singer has a delicate voice.
She carried a heavy load on her slender shoulders.
She looks slight, but she's strong.
She spoke in a faintly trembling voice.
My fingers are slender, so rings are too big.
The frail child has become healthy before I knew it.

explain: 몸이나 목소리, 줄기가 가늘고 연약해 보일 때 써요. '날씬하다'와 달리 약하고 섬세해 보이는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '가녀린 몸', '가녀린 목소리'처럼 사람이나 식물에 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a body, voice or stem that is thin and looks fragile. Unlike '날씬하다' (slim), it carries a feeling of being delicate and weak. It is typically used as in '가녀린 몸' and '가녀린 목소리', for people or plants.

examples.en: Please don't say such ridiculous things.

examples.ko: 아무 노력도 없이 일등을 바라다니 가당찮아요.
examples.en: Hoping for first place without any effort is absurd.
People thought his plan was preposterous.
My friend laughed and said my request was out of the question.
The price was outrageous, so I just left.
Telling me to be satisfied with that is simply unreasonable.

explain: 어이없고 이치에 맞지 않는다고 할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 주로 '가당찮은 소리/요구/생각'처럼 말해요. '가당치 않다'의 준말이고 둘 다 써요.
explain_en: You use this when something is outrageous or makes no sense. It mostly appears as '가당찮은 소리', '가당찮은 요구' or '가당찮은 생각'. It is a shortened form of '가당치 않다', and both are used.

examples.en: I'm already busy, and now more work has come up.
It's already cold today, and now it's raining too.
I'm already late, and the road is jammed too.

examples.ko: 저는 가뜩이나 기분이 안 좋은데 그런 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: I was already in a bad mood, and then I heard that.
I'm already broke, and I even lost my wallet.

examples.ko: 시험 때문에 가뜩이나 힘든 아이에게 잔소리하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't nag a kid who is already struggling with exams.

explain: 안 좋은 상황에 또 나쁜 일이 겹칠 때 써요. 보통 '가뜩이나' 꼴로 쓰고, 좋은 일이 겹칠 때는 안 맞아요. '안 그래도'와 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: You use it when something bad is added to an already bad situation. It is usually used in the form '가뜩이나', and doesn't fit when good things pile up. It works much like '안 그래도' (already, as it is).
